title: Chapter 2: Towns and Signals
summary: Follow the light beam down a road-movie stretch of highway. Scavenge two empty towns for supplies; the RV becomes your mobile base. Gas and antibiotics run low; a mystery signal hits the pager. Ringo and Xian's resolve quietly shifts as the broadcast tower comes into view for the first time.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Dawn on the second day. Light peels up from the horizon like faded gray cloth. The RV still chases the crackle on the radio—static, and something that sounds like someone breathing far away.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: In the back seat, Xian has her face turned to the window, breathing quick and shallow. The antibiotics are running out, but the road keeps getting longer. The fuel gauge sits low and ugly, like a needle about to snap.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: ...I counted. Six cans left, two and a half cases of water. Antibiotics—counting what we used last night—four doses.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Miles spreads a crumpled map across his knees and marks X's beside town names. Every X is somewhere they passed through or gave up on. His hand stays steady when he writes the numbers, like it's one small thing he can still control.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The first town shows up beside the highway. Faded signs, intact shop windows—like someone hit pause. Wind cuts through empty streets and blows an old newspaper into the road, then lets it settle.

scenes.speaker: ringo
scenes.text: Resupply first. Don't drive at night.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Ringo eases off the gas. The RV tires crunch gravel, loud in the dead quiet. In the rearview, the highway looks like a thin thread you've already left behind—there isn't much room to go back.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The corner pharmacy's windows are shattered. Sunlight slants through the gaps and scatters across powdered glass. A few pill boxes still sit on the shelves, labels curled from damp.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: But there are fresh footprints on the floor—from the door to the back room, stopping by scattered pill boxes, then heading out again. Someone got here before you, and not long ago.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: ...Tracks go inward. No drag marks. Probably one person—or at least someone who can still walk on their own.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: Give me a bag. I'll search the back. Don't spread out too far.

scenes.speaker: ringo
scenes.text: ...I'll watch the door. Move fast.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Ringo backs against the doorframe, crowbar across her chest. Her eyes sweep the street across the way—an old gas station sign, red paint peeling bad, like a scar that never healed right. She doesn't look at it long.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Time's short. Gas is dripping away while you idle. You need to decide how to scavenge this town.

interactive.objective: [Objective] Town 1 · Pharmacy run: choose your approach
suggestions: Ringo and I go in. Xian stays in the RV.
I'll sweep it fast alone. You two guard the vehicle.
Circle the building first—check those footprints before we touch anything.
interactive.aiGoal: Town 1 scavenge decision. Ringo hesitates briefly because of the gas station (ties to her guilt). Miles can help carry and count meds. Finish the run with a small antibiotics haul. No firefights or new characters. Everyone returns to the RV after.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Miles hauls out half a crate of unexpired antibiotics and a few bottles of disinfectant, tying the bag tight like he's afraid the last bit of hope might spill out. Drawers in the back room were rifled through—but nobody's there.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: That'll hold us for a while. ...I'll split the disinfectant into smaller bottles. Easier on the road.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Ringo's hands still shake a little when she tosses the meds into the RV. She doesn't say a word. Miles takes them, sets them down, and casually blocks the door with his shoulder—maybe on accident, maybe so she catches less wind.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Scavenge done—you don't linger. The RV pulls out of town and stops at the roadside. New rule: grab what you need and go. No sleeping in empty cities.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: In the weeds off the highway, flattened grass forms a half-circle—other travelers stopped here too, once. Ringo kills the engine. Suddenly it's just wind on the roof and distant bugs. These days, even bug noise feels like a luxury.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: I'll change Xian's dressing. You guys... who wants to sleep first?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Miles unscrews the disinfectant, moving softer than he speaks. He brushes sweat from Xian's forehead, checks her temperature, then slowly lifts the old bandage. Xian's brow tightens—but she doesn't pull away. That's trust, right there.

scenes.speaker: xian
scenes.text: ...So loud. Your voices... like needles.

scenes.speaker: ringo
scenes.text: Then I'll keep it down. ...No, I'll just stop. Get some sleep.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: It's okay. I'll go slower. ...If it hurts, grab my sleeve. Don't bite your lip.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The RV bakes at night, a metal box with the lid on. Xian's forehead is scarily hot. Ringo sits in the driver's seat pretending to watch the road—except the road is right there and her heart's stuck in the back. Miles folds the used bandage neat, knuckles white from the pressure.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: She needs to hear something that'll get her to morning.

interactive.objective: [Objective] RV at night: steady Ringo, get Xian to accept the dressing change
interactive.playerPrompt: What do you tell your friends?
suggestions: Ringo, you've done enough. We'll find more meds at dawn.
Xian, this dose'll help—you won't feel as bad. I'm right here.
I'll take watch tonight. You two rest.
interactive.aiGoal: RV night talk. Xian's pain is back; she resists treatment (resolve 0→30 arc). Ringo blames herself but holds it together. Miles helps with the dressing and short comfort. After the player reassures them, Xian grudgingly accepts; Ringo loosens up a little. Don't jump to the tower or any ending.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Third day, early. Thin mist slides along the ground. You're on the road again. Xian looks a little better than last night—just a little, like one crack of light in a gray sky.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: Fever's down a bit. I checked. ...Think we can find more meds today?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Nobody answers. Ringo just shifts gears and keeps the throttle steady. Up ahead the highway splits and merges again, like punctuation that can't make up its mind.

scenes.speaker: ringo
scenes.text: Fuel gauge... not great. Next place to fill up might be a long way.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Up ahead, a bigger gas station complex—convenience store and auto shop attached. The sign's still up, but the colors have faded into the same tired gray. Radio static spikes here—like someone's talking nearby, or the tower is breathing.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: You slow down. The convenience store's automatic door hangs half-open, wind knocking it back and forth. In the garage, a dusty tire swings from a chain like an abandoned pendulum.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: I'll check the underground tanks first. Don't get too close—this place... doesn't feel right.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Gas is almost gone. Only a few antibiotic doses left. You have to choose: hunt for fuel or follow the signal.

interactive.objective: [Objective] Supply crisis: fuel first, or chase the signal?
suggestions: Search the gas station first. Without fuel we go nowhere.
The signal's strongest here—follow it. We'll deal with gas later.
Split up: Ringo hauls fuel, I'll hit the convenience store.
interactive.aiGoal: Gas crisis decision. Whatever the player picks, barely scrape together fuel (+1 or +2). Miles can siphon or scavenge the store. Time passes; Xian stays in bad shape. You can mention a tower silhouette in the distance. Don't enter the tower top or any ending.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The underground tanks still have some settled gas. Miles sticks in the siphon, forearms streaked with fuel, and sucks without a word—chokes on the first pull, turns aside to cough twice, then keeps going.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: Enough to reach the next town. ...Not more than that. I measured.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: By the time the cans are full, the sun's low. On the horizon, a thin silhouette flickers in the dusk—tower, or a spike driven into the sky.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Behind the convenience store counter, an old pager blinks in the dark. The screen lights green on dusty glass and spits out a line: "Are you looking for Teacher too?"

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: ...Could be a trap. Could be real. Would Teacher... leave a message like this?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Miles doesn't touch the pager—just stands a step back. The indicator blinks on and off, lighting all four faces in turn, like some old stubborn Q&A.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: No signature on the signal. The pager light keeps blinking, waiting for your reply.

interactive.objective: [Objective] Pager signal: reply to the stranger (start async contact)
suggestions: We lost our adults too. Which way are you?
Cut the mystery—if you want to team up, send coordinates.
interactive.aiGoal: Pager interaction. The other party is a mystery survivor (not on-screen yet; don't use a male crew name). Miles can express cautious hope nearby. Replies should be vague, friendly, or wary, with a hint to head toward the radio tower. Can mention they're looking for Teacher too. Don't reveal identity or jump to the tower top.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: A few seconds later, the pager spits out a second line: "Head north. The tower's lit. ...Don't give up on the one with the camera." Then the screen goes dark, like comfort offered and taken back.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: ...It knows about Xian. At least, the camera. Maybe someone really is up ahead.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: After you leave the gas station, the radio static clears for a second. A flat voice repeats coordinate-like numbers, then the wind swallows it again. Headlights paint the highway like an old tape played too many times.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: I wrote down the frequency. In case we pick it up again...

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: He tears off a corner of the map, pencils down the numbers, folds it, and slides it into the dash. Ringo catches him in the rearview and says nothing. From the back comes Xian's steady breathing—or what you choose to believe is steady.

scenes.speaker: ringo
scenes.text: I'm not a great captain. But... as long as you're still on this bus, I'll keep driving.

scenes.speaker: xian
scenes.text: ...In the viewfinder, the tower's closer than yesterday. Not a hallucination.

scenes.speaker: miles
scenes.text: Then let's go. ...Honestly, no other road feels more right anyway.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Dusk washes the wasteland old-copper. Wind pours through open windows, dust and a faint metallic smell—rust, or blood.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: On the horizon, a radio tower cuts into the dusk. The pager, the radio static, the light in Xian's camera—all of it points there.

interactive.objective: [Objective] Chapter 2 finale: floor it toward the broadcast tower?
suggestions: Full speed. Get to the tower before Xian can't hold on.
Stop somewhere for the night. Charge at it tomorrow.
Ringo, drive toward the signal. I trust what Xian saw.
interactive.aiGoal: Chapter 2 wrap-up. However the player wavers, they commit to the broadcast tower. Ringo grips the wheel; Miles straightens the back; Xian clutches her camera. Don't enter the tower top, campfire, or any ending.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The RV takes the last bend. The broadcast tower stands at the edge of the wasteland, red light pulsing slow, like a heart. Chapter 2 ends here—what's at the base of the tower, nobody can say.

notes: Matches Figma: scavenge → back to RV → keep moving; pager async contact; gas/antibiotics crisis; resolve growth setup. Miles joins scavenge runs, night care, and pager reactions. Middle town nodes are author placeholders; this chapter uses two functional stops (pharmacy town + gas station complex).
